title: The Remote — Sc108: forced-perspective run (giant Darwin FG, small Gumball BG)

source.github: mhvnsnt/cn-gigaleak-gumball, draft release untagged-1676e192ae8c72e95791, asset id 640772406
source.method: FLA (XFL zip) read via sequential local-header parser (2012 Flash zips have malformed central directory); DOMDocument.xml + LIBRARY symbol XMLs parsed directly. Same neutral per-keyframe transform format as production/dance-choreo v1: a part pose is (item, first_frame, affine matrix a/b/c/d/tx/ty, pivot). keyMode 9728 = pose-to-pose; sampled_frames hold each keyframe's elements to the next keyframe, matching SWF playback.

teaches: Locomotion + forced perspective: both characters run library cycles ('gb run cycle' 410 kf, 'dar run cycle' 223 kf), but the staging does the work — Darwin's cycle is placed HUGE in the foreground, cropped by the frame edge, one giant leg swinging across the shot, while Gumball runs the same kind of cycle small in the background clutching the remote. The background is reduced to a horizontal speed smear: no location detail at all. Travel, scale comedy and near-collision (Darwin's foot swings past Gumball ~frame 23) all come from placement scale, not new drawings.
notes: Same asset class, two scales: a cycle symbol reads completely differently at 0.3x (background) vs 3x cropped (foreground).
The 'background' layer is a speed-line smear — at full run, location is deleted on purpose.
Darwin's foreground leg overlaps Gumball's space on the swing: FG/BG characters share the frame's depth, staged by layer order (GB layer + Darwin over).
40 frames total: just enough loops for the cut; the cycles do the rest.
